svg.text: Every box is a real module. Paths are repository-relative. Open this file at excalidraw.com to pan, zoom and edit.
1 · The system: where the rules actually live
One rule: the room decides. A browser can ask for anything; the engine that answers is the one on the server.
No React. No socket. No clock of its own.
Same input → same output, every time.
2 · A clue's life — the engine's state machine
src/lib/game/clue-flow.ts. Every arrow is a command the room accepted; the dashed ones are the clock.
skip → next round if the board is bare
The clock does the same work nobody pressed a button for:
· nobody wagered → stake the minimum and read the clue
· nobody rang in → close the window, show the answer
· everyone who owes an answer has sent one → reveal at once
· ruled on and idle → clear the clue, roll the round over
1,578 lines in one file became five that each answer one question.
may they? who picks? what's it worth?
pick → wager → buzz → judge → skip · tick
dispatchGameCommand is a lookup table, not a switch:
Adding a command is one line, and nothing can fall through.
Every handler is the same two moves:
The guard ladders that used to open each one are now a table.
4 · One room, two ways to run it
Solo play runs the room in your tab; a shared room runs it in a Durable Object. Same RoomHost either way, so rules and pacing match exactly.
A dropped socket keeps your seat and your score until you come back;
leaving on purpose hands the seat back. The host chair always belongs
to somebody who is actually in the room (room-flow.ts · ensureHost).
5 · From the archive to the board
one clue shape, whatever came in
The board draws a clue in the row its value names, and an empty blue
cell where the archive has none — 30% of archived rounds are short
The board is a grid of one Cell component: a category strip, a value you
can press, a square the archive never had, and the ghost board before a
game is dealt are the same rectangle with different text.
board / gold / clue face — the set itself, untouched
ui.* stage, surface, line, ink, blue, gold — the studio around it
controls.* housing · readout · key · keyPrimary · buzzer · keyOff
displayType() clueType() clueScale() — the three recipes every screen uses
